paragraphs.title: Bezalel Called for the Holy Work

easy.question: Whom did the Lord call by name to carry out the work of the tabernacle?
easy.explanation: The Lord told Moses that He had called Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, by name.

easy.question: Which tribe was Bezalel from?
easy.explanation: Bezalel was from the tribe of Judah.

easy.question: What materials was Bezalel required to work with?
easy.explanation: The verses mention working with gold, silver, and brass.

medium.question: Why did the Lord fill Bezalel with the spirit of God, wisdom, understanding, and knowledge?
answers: So he could skillfully carry out various kinds of work
So he could become king over Israel
So he could lead the people in the wilderness
medium.explanation: These qualities enabled Bezalel to devise skillful works and make the tabernacle.

medium.question: What was Aholiab’s role in relation to Bezalel?
answers: To work alongside him on the tabernacle
To guard the holy vessels alone
medium.explanation: The Lord appointed Aholiab with Bezalel, and together they were to make all that the Lord commanded.

medium.question: In the phrase “in cutting of stones, to set them,” what does “to set them” mean?
answers: To place stones in their proper settings
medium.explanation: The phrase describes shaping stones and setting them into a fitting place, such as in a piece of jewelry or a sacred object.

challenge.question: What can we learn from the fact that Bezalel was from Judah and Aholiab was from Dan?
answers: The tabernacle work involved people from different tribes
Only people from Judah worked on the tabernacle
challenge.explanation: The verses identify each man’s tribe, showing that the work brought together people from different tribes.

challenge.question: What does the repeated phrase “all manner of workmanship” show about Bezalel’s abilities?
answers: He knew only how to work with wood
He had a wide range of skills in different crafts
He only planned the work and did not carry it out
challenge.explanation: The phrase, together with the list of materials and crafts, emphasizes the breadth of his abilities.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the Lord did not give skill in craftsmanship only to Bezalel?
answers: Bezalel was the son of Uri
Aholiab was from the tribe of Dan
Wisdom was also given to everyone who was wise-hearted
challenge.explanation: Verse 6 says that wisdom was also placed in the hearts of all who were wise-hearted, so Bezalel was not the only skilled worker.

questions.question: What can we learn from the fact that Bezalel was from Judah and Aholiab was from Dan?
answers: The tabernacle work involved people from different tribes
Only people from Judah worked on the tabernacle
questions.explanation: The verses identify each man’s tribe, showing that the work brought together people from different tribes.

questions.question: What does the repeated phrase “all manner of workmanship” show about Bezalel’s abilities?
answers: He knew only how to work with wood
He had a wide range of skills in different crafts
He only planned the work and did not carry it out
questions.explanation: The phrase, together with the list of materials and crafts, emphasizes the breadth of his abilities.

answers: Bezalel was the son of Uri

Wisdom was also given to everyone who was wise-hearted
questions.explanation: Verse 6 says that wisdom was also placed in the hearts of all who were wise-hearted, so Bezalel was not the only skilled worker.

paragraphs.title: The Tabernacle Furniture and Holy Garments

easy.question: Which item is mentioned in verse 7?
easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “the ark of the testimony.”

easy.question: For whom were the holy garments in verse 10 intended?
easy.explanation: The verse mentions holy garments for Aaron the priest and garments for his sons to serve as priests.

easy.question: What is mentioned together with the laver?
easy.explanation: Verse 9 says, “the laver and his foot.”

medium.question: Which item was mentioned first in the list?
medium.explanation: The altar of incense appears in verse 8, before the altar of burnt offering and the laver in verse 9.

medium.question: In the phrase “the cloths of service,” what are “cloths of service”?
answers: Garments used in the holy service
medium.explanation: The context of the tabernacle furnishings and priestly garments shows that these were garments used in sacred service.

medium.question: What instruction is given concerning all the things listed?
answers: They must make everything as the Lord commanded
They should choose only the most important items
They should prepare them only after entering the land
medium.explanation: The passage ends by saying, “according to all that I have commanded thee shall they do.”

challenge.question: Which item does not appear in verse 8?
challenge.explanation: Verse 8 mentions the table, the candlestick, and the altar of incense; the laver appears in verse 9.

challenge.question: What appears in the list immediately after the candlestick and its furniture?
challenge.explanation: Immediately after the candlestick and all its furniture, the passage says, “the altar of incense.”

challenge.question: What does “that is thereupon” refer to in the phrase “the mercy seat that is thereupon”?
challenge.explanation: The mercy seat was upon the ark, which is mentioned immediately before it.

questions.question: Which item does not appear in verse 8?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 mentions the table, the candlestick, and the altar of incense; the laver appears in verse 9.

questions.question: What appears in the list immediately after the candlestick and its furniture?
questions.explanation: Immediately after the candlestick and all its furniture, the passage says, “the altar of incense.”

questions.question: What does “that is thereupon” refer to in the phrase “the mercy seat that is thereupon”?
questions.explanation: The mercy seat was upon the ark, which is mentioned immediately before it.

paragraphs.title: Keeping the Sabbath as a Covenant Sign

easy.question: Which day of the week is called “the sabbath of rest”?
easy.explanation: Verse 15 says, “in the seventh is the sabbath of rest, holy to the Lord.”

easy.question: What were the children of Israel commanded to do on the Sabbath?
easy.explanation: The verses repeatedly command the children of Israel to keep the Sabbath.

easy.question: Between whom is the Sabbath a sign?
answers: Between the priests and the people
Between the Lord and the children of Israel
easy.explanation: The Sabbath is described as a sign between the Lord and the children of Israel.

medium.question: Why were the children of Israel to keep the Sabbath throughout their generations?
answers: Because it was a perpetual covenant and a sign between them and the Lord
So they could work all week
Because it was intended only for the wilderness generation
medium.explanation: The Sabbath is called a perpetual covenant and a sign between the Lord and Israel, so it was intended for all generations.

medium.question: In the phrase “every one that defileth it,” what does “defileth it” mean?
answers: Whoever dishonors or violates the holiness of the Sabbath
Whoever announces the beginning of the Sabbath
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to anyone who profanes the Sabbath; the following words describe the severe punishment for doing so.

medium.question: Which sequence correctly describes the week according to these verses?
answers: Six days of work followed by a day of rest
One day of work followed by six days of rest
medium.explanation: Verse 15 says, “Six days may work be done; but in the seventh is the sabbath of rest.”

challenge.question: What connection between the Sabbath and creation is emphasized in verse 17?
answers: The Sabbath was intended only to remember the exodus from Egypt
The Sabbath is connected with the Lord’s making heaven and earth in six days and resting on the seventh
The Sabbath was intended to commemorate the building of the tabernacle
challenge.explanation: The verse connects the six days of work with the six days of creation and the Sabbath with the Lord’s rest on the seventh day.

challenge.question: What can we conclude from the repetition of the word “sign” in verses 13 and 17?
answers: The Sabbath is a continuing sign of the special relationship between the Lord and Israel
The Sabbath is a sign that all days are equal
The Sabbath is a sign of Moses’ dwelling place
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that the Sabbath is not merely a break from work but a lasting sign of the covenant and relationship between the Lord and Israel.

challenge.question: Which wording especially emphasizes that the Sabbath was not intended for only one generation?
answers: The words “throughout their generations” and “for ever”
challenge.explanation: These words show that keeping the Sabbath was to continue through all generations and forever.

paragraphs.title: The Tables of Testimony at Mount Sinai

easy.question: Who gave Moses the tables of testimony?
easy.explanation: The verse says that God gave Moses the tables.

easy.question: Where did Moses receive the tables?
easy.explanation: The verse says this happened on Mount Sinai.

easy.question: What were the tables made of?
easy.explanation: The verse describes them as tables of stone.

medium.question: When did God give Moses the tables?
answers: After He had finished speaking with Moses
Before Moses went up the mountain
After Moses came down from the mountain
medium.explanation: The verse says, “when he had made an end of communing with him,” meaning after God had finished speaking with Moses.

medium.question: What is the connection between the “tables of testimony” and the writing on them?
answers: The writing on them expressed the testimony they carried
They were used to build the tabernacle
medium.explanation: They were called tables of testimony, and they bore testimony written by God.

medium.question: In the phrase “when he had made an end of communing with him,” what does “made an end” mean?
medium.explanation: The phrase means that God had finished speaking with Moses.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by the phrase “written with the finger of God”?
answers: The writing is attributed directly to God
The tables were written with fire
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the writing came directly from God rather than being produced by human hands.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the word “two” in the description of the tables?
answers: There were two kinds of materials
challenge.explanation: The word shows that two tables were given together as a pair.

challenge.question: Which detail especially reinforces the holiness of the tables?
answers: They were written with the finger of God
challenge.explanation: Attributing the writing to God especially reinforces the sacred and unique status of the tables.

questions.question: What is emphasized by the phrase “written with the finger of God”?
answers: The writing is attributed directly to God
The tables were written with fire
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the writing came directly from God rather than being produced by human hands.

questions.explanation: The word shows that two tables were given together as a pair.

questions.explanation: Attributing the writing to God especially reinforces the sacred and unique status of the tables.
